meta_webhook_bug_found_and_fixed.summary: The /api/ingestion/meta/<token> callback route only accepted POST. Meta's Webhooks product sends its GET verification challenge to the same registered callback URL used for POST delivery, not a separate path, so every attempt to register the app-level webhook subscription failed with HTTP 405 before Meta could validate it. This is very likely why webhook delivery had been silent since 22 July, independent of the OAuth token issue.
meta_webhook_bug_found_and_fixed.fix: Route now accepts GET and POST; GET delegates to the existing, already-correct meta_verify handler. POST delivery logic unchanged.
meta_webhook_bug_found_and_fixed.verified: Meta App Dashboard Webhooks (Page object) Callback URL + Verify token saved successfully; leadgen field subscribed; one real test lead sent via Meta's Lead Ads Testing Tool was received, signature-validated, correctly routed to source 12 by page_id, and logged with a correct correlation ID and idempotency key in ingested_lead_logs (id 4442). The only remaining failure on that test lead is 'Lead payload missing name or contact method', because Meta webhook payloads only carry IDs and the enrichment call to fetch full lead details still needs a valid Page token.

meta_oauth_status: all four sources (11,12,13,14) confirmed INVALID via live Graph API re-check as of 15:20 IST, code 190 / subcode 460 ('session invalidated because the user changed their password or Facebook has changed the session for security reasons'). Owner confirmed no account compromise (only own devices in active sessions, password-change timestamp matches owner's own action). Two clean reconnect attempts (13:49 and 14:19 IST) each produced tokens that worked for a moment (successfully re-subscribed the Page webhook) then died again within minutes with the identical error. Most likely explanation: a Meta-side post-password-change security cooldown affecting third-party app tokens specifically (web login session stays valid throughout). Recommend waiting several hours before the next attempt rather than continuing immediate retries.

cron_job_org_drift_found_and_corrected.summary: Live cron-job.org console showed 'LMS - Meta Lead Poll' and 'LMS - Meta Report Sync' actively running every 5 minutes, contradicting the release report's certification that both were inactive. These are legacy/duplicate paths: Meta Lead Poll re-fetches leads that should arrive via webhook, and Meta Report Sync duplicates the Vercel-owned once-daily spend sync at a much higher frequency. Both were hammering the Graph API with the same tokens every 5 minutes, a plausible contributor to the OAuth session churn.
cron_job_org_drift_found_and_corrected.action_taken: Owner disabled both jobs directly in the cron-job.org console during this session.
